items.prompt: Use case: scientific-educational. A clean original 3D artist pose reference sheet. Adult gender-neutral mannequin, average balanced proportions. Featureless smooth matte light-gray oval head, no facial features, no hair. Wearing plain opaque warm-gray long-sleeve crewneck practice shirt, straight full-length trousers, and simple gray cloth shoes. Clothes have modest natural ease, not a skin suit; hands are matte gray simplified mannequin hands with correct fingers. Minimal realistic 3D studio rendering, soft shading. A frozen natural walking stride, LEFT foot forward with heel touching the ground, RIGHT foot behind with heel raised, RIGHT arm slightly forward and LEFT arm back. Keep this exact gait and limb laterality in every view. EXACT equal 2 by 2 grid of the SAME SINGLE frozen pose: top left true FRONT camera, top right front 45-degree THREE-QUARTER camera, bottom left true RIGHT SIDE profile camera, bottom right true BACK camera. Camera rotates; mannequin and props DO NOT change posture or swap limbs. All four views share proportions, hand contacts and prop geometry. Whole figure from crown to shoe soles and all props fully inside each quadrant with 8 percent blank margins and broad blank center gutters. Camera at neutral body-height, no foreshortened extreme angles. Plain warm ivory background and subtle grounding shadow. No captions, text, borders, divider lines, arrows, extra people, historical garments, ornaments or scenery. All limbs intact and naturally supported. This is a movement reference, not a finished historical costume portrait.

Do not copy reference patterned silk, coat shape, actor, weapon, accessories or hat. Do not introduce embroidery, extra layers, insignia or designs. Remove boots entirely; no person, skin or support. items.prompt: Use case: precise-object-edit. Image 1 is the existing EMPTY garment four-view sheet to edit; image 2 is the selected television COSTUME COLOR reference. References establish visible color distribution, not an exact historical reconstruction. Preserve the edit target's cut, seams, length, garment layers, gender proportions, fabric weight, and original decoration unless explicitly instructed. Do not add insignia or increase decorative rank. Pure empty clothing only: no person, skin, face, neck, hands, feet, mannequin, hanger or visible support. Remove any empty shoes if present. Hollow openings show textile lining only. EXACT square 2x2 equal panels showing ONE identical outfit: top-left FRONT, top-right front THREE-QUARTER, bottom-left strict SIDE, bottom-right BACK. Complete garment in every panel, generous central blank gutters and 10 percent margins. All four views must have identical colors and construction. Clean ivory studio background, neutral soft light, clearly readable cloth grain, controlled silk sheen where appropriate; no grey fog, sepia cast or theatrical lighting. No text, borders, logos or scenery. Never include the reference actor or accessories. Back and hidden surfaces are coherent design extensions, not documented reconstruction. Use the standing man in the selected Legend of Kublai Khan reference: rich very dark chocolate near-black front and back robe panels with the targets EXISTING motifs rendered in warm clear gold, warm chestnut-brown sleeves and side panels, narrow light champagne-gold collar/edge trim, and a gold-brown belt. Do not copy the reference cut, do not add an open overcoat. Preserve the target ONE closed asymmetric narrow-sleeve Mongol-style long robe and its existing decorative motif placement, waist construction, lining and winter padding if present. Do not add a new dragon or new insignia. Avoid flat mustard-yellow fabric across the whole outfit; show the reference contrast between dark gold-woven main panels and warm brown sleeves. FLAT textile embroidery, not a realistic zoo lion, not a Western heraldic lion, no bird, no dragon, no text. Same coherent badge on front and back, undivided square on front, never split like a Qing center-opening coat. This is a sourced creative reference for Ming first/second-rank military officials' regular official dress, not a certified reconstruction.

items.prompt: Use case: precise-object-edit. Image 1 is the EDIT TARGET Qing official summer hat four-view sheet. Image 2 is the SELECTED Yongzheng Dynasty reference of officials in summer hats. Keep the target standalone hollow conical woven hat silhouette and its small simple red bead finial as an illustrative, non-rank-specific detail. Refine coarse straw to fine pale ivory-cream woven fiber; extend finer clear red silk tassels from the finial further down toward the lower brim, leaving a narrow pale woven band visible above a thin black edge. Completely REMOVE the large red chin loop, central knot and hanging tassel below the brim in ALL FOUR PANELS: source reference shows no large dangling chin ornament. No human, face, head, hair, neck, shoulders, mannequin or display support. No peacock feather, imperial dragon, added jewels or gold court-rank emblems. EXACT equal 2x2 grid of ONE object: FRONT top-left, front THREE-QUARTER top-right, SIDE bottom-left, BACK bottom-right. Identical red bead and cap construction in all views, hollow dark underside where visible. Ivory studio background, neutral soft light, natural textile grain, complete silhouette with generous blank central gutters. No labels, borders or watermark. Underside and back are design extensions; the red finial is illustrative because the main reference finial is cropped.
